strengths: Well-motivated 3D extension of Field of Junctions with elegant geometric parameterization using intersecting planes
Comprehensive multi-domain experimental validation across CT, cryo-ET, and point cloud denoising with consistent strong performance
Exceptional robustness at extreme low-SNR conditions (F50, F100) while preserving sharp edges and fine structures better than neural and classical alternatives
Training-free approach avoids hallucination issues inherent in neural networks, particularly valuable for domains with limited clean data
Clear mathematical formulation, detailed algorithms, comprehensive appendices, and transparent hyperparameter reporting enhance reproducibility
Demonstrates that simple geometric priors can remain competitive with learned neural methods across diverse imaging modalities
weaknesses: Limited core novelty: extending 2D FoJ to 3D through plane parameterization is relatively incremental both mathematically and conceptually

Overstated 'training-free' claim: method requires careful tuning of multiple hyperparameters (patch size, stride, regions M, smoothness η/δ, weights λ_B/λ_C) with insufficient practical guidance for new domains
Incomplete comparisons with neural methods: missing recent deep learning baselines for CT and cryo-ET; point cloud comparisons use outdated methods (2021-2023)
No quantitative ground-truth validation for real cryo-ET data; evaluation relies on subjective visual inspection, undermining claims of superiority
Convergence analysis absent: non-convex optimization lacks theoretical guarantees, convergence proof, or local minima discussion
Scalability and computational efficiency underexplored: testing limited to 512³ volumes; memory requirements, runtime scaling, and GPU efficiency comparisons with neural methods missing
Point cloud results suboptimal: voxelization to 256³ may discard sparse data information; performance only competitive (not superior) to PointCVaR at high noise
Limited failure mode analysis: no discussion of problem types where junction parameterization is insufficient or whether method works on highly anisotropic/textured volumes
Incomplete ablation studies: no separate analysis of fidelity vs. boundary vs. consistency terms; interaction effects between hyperparameters underexplored
Implicit regularization mechanism unexplained: theoretical justification for why this parameterization generalizes across domains is missing

strengths: Training-free method avoids hallucination risks and enables application across diverse volumetric imaging modalities without retraining
Comprehensive experimental validation across three applications (CT, cryo-ET, point clouds) with extensive comparisons to classical, untrained neural, and trained denoiser baselines
Strong empirical results, particularly robust at extreme low-SNR conditions while preserving fine structural details
Thorough ablation studies on hyperparameters, convergence analysis, and computational cost evaluation
Technically sound formulation with proper mathematical framework and clear algorithmic description supporting reproducibility
Well-presented paper with effective organization, clear figures, and detailed experimental tables
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty - core contribution is relatively straightforward 3D extension of existing 2D Field of Junctions method, representing incremental rather than fundamental contribution

Incomplete hyperparameter sensitivity analysis - multiple tunable parameters (M, patch size, stride, η, δ) with limited guidance for practitioners; Section 10.5 reveals significant performance dependence on these choices for curved structures
Computational cost not adequately justified - requires 11.3-18.5 minutes for moderate-sized volumes, slower than neural networks, without clear articulation of when this tradeoff is worthwhile
Limited theoretical understanding - no convergence guarantees, approximation error bounds, or analysis of representable structure classes; only empirical stability claimed
Narrow scope of applicability - all experiments involve piecewise-smooth structures; acknowledged poor performance on highly curved geometries; generalization to complex non-smooth structures unclear

Incomplete baseline comparisons - untrained neural priors likely use default hyperparameters rather than careful tuning; some 2D baselines may not be optimally adapted to 3D; missing recent deep learning methods
Mixed results on cryo-ET where SC-Net sometimes matches or exceeds 3D FoJ performance, undermining claims of geometric modeling superiority
Insufficient practical guidance - no decision criteria provided for when to choose 3D FoJ over alternatives; applicability conditions not clearly delineated
